title: A mechanistic correlate that predicts human protection from a new virus

concept.text: The proposed innovation is an immune measurement, coupled to a pre-specified prediction rule, that reliably forecasts whether a vaccine will protect people against a newly emerging virus. It would provide useful evidence before clinical protection outcomes are known, including for a virus that lacked an accepted correlate when the measurement was proposed. The intended advance includes portability across viral families, with the boundaries of that portability established through testing.

Protection must have a defined meaning: preventing infection, reducing onward transmission, preventing symptomatic illness and preventing severe disease or death are different outcomes. An immune measurement that predicts one cannot automatically be used for the others. Beeton and Case's 2026 review explains why this distinction matters for respiratory vaccination: immunity measured in circulation may poorly represent protection at the respiratory surface, and mucosal correlates may depend on both the pathogen and the vaccine platform.

Conceptual distinction: a predictive correlate forecasts outcomes; a mechanistic correlate also has evidence connecting the measured immune state causally to protection. A measurement could predict protection because it tracks another protective process, without itself identifying the mechanism. Completing this innovation therefore requires both prospective predictive performance and a convincing biological explanation of why the measurement indicates protection.

significance.text: Reliable early prediction could substantially reduce uncertainty in outbreak vaccine development. It could help researchers select promising regimens, identify ineffective ones and produce evidence relevant to deployment decisions before all clinical protection outcomes have accumulated. CEPI's Bundibugyo account illustrates the opportunity: rapid contracting, manufacturing and initial clinical development coexisted with outstanding late-stage efficacy and immune-response assessment constraints.

The direct scientific benefit would be earlier, better-grounded evidence about protection. Earlier deployment would remain conditional on adequate safety evidence, regulatory acceptance, manufacturing, financing, surveillance and delivery. CEPI explicitly describes the need for regulatory, financing and access pathways to advance alongside trials. Even a highly informative protection measurement would address only part of that response.

Conditional synthesis: successful transfer across tested viral families could make preparedness more reusable, reducing the amount of protection-prediction work that must begin from scratch during an outbreak. The analogy to a common measuring ruler has limits: its calibration could still depend on the endpoint, population, vaccine platform and biological setting. The capability would reduce empirical uncertainty; it would not establish safety, guarantee deployment or universally replace disease-endpoint trials.

The supplied evidence does not justify describing vaccine development generally as a multi-year gamble or claiming that efficacy trials cannot fit within expanding epidemics. Beeton and Case discuss the development of safe and effective SARS-CoV-2 vaccines in less than a year. The transformative claim here is therefore the prospect of more reliable early prediction across new settings, rather than the assertion that rapid clinical development is otherwise impossible.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability is rapid establishment of an immune measurement that prospectively predicts clinically meaningful human protection for a new virus, with demonstrated mechanism and tested transfer beyond a single setting. The supplied materials document important pieces of this gap, particularly unresolved mucosal correlates, but do not establish that every emerging virus lacks an applicable correlate or that no relevant portable approach exists anywhere in the field.

One biological barrier is determining which immune compartment and response matter for the chosen endpoint. A circulating antibody response may be informative about some forms of protection while inadequately representing respiratory-surface immunity or transmission control. Pathogen and vaccine-platform dependence complicate transfer: a measurement calibrated for one vaccine or virus may not retain the same interpretation for another. Beeton and Case identify reproducible, standardized correlates as unfinished work and specifically discuss continuing difficulties for live-attenuated influenza vaccines.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: researchers must separate a causal protective process from an associated marker, establish a reliable assay and translate its result into a prediction with quantified uncertainty. They must then determine how that relationship changes across populations, regimens, platforms and viruses. Assay reproducibility alone would not establish biological transferability, and an accurate prediction alone would not establish mechanism.

Outbreak use adds a timing barrier. CEPI identifies rapid immune-response assessment as a constraint in the Bundibugyo response, alongside later-stage testing and operational readiness. Measuring an immune response quickly is only an enabling step: the harder requirement is showing that the measured response predicts protection well enough to inform a decision while the outbreak is still unfolding.

current_state.text: In their CEPI account dated 25 August 2026, Lurie and Kelland report vaccine-development contracts within two weeks and production by Serum Institute of India of enough drug substance for initial trials of Oxford University's ChAdOx Bundibugyo candidate in 14 days. First Phase 1 participants were dosed 80 days after the first reported Bundibugyo case in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. These are early-development milestones; they do not establish clinical protection.

At the 100-day emergency milestone described by CEPI, there was no approved vaccine specifically against Bundibugyo, matched candidates remained in Phase 1 and later-stage efficacy testing was still being prepared. The two timing references have different starting points: the 80-day dosing interval begins with the first reported case, whereas the 100-day milestone begins with the emergency declaration. The account documents outstanding efficacy constraints in this response; it does not provide a general quantitative comparison showing that efficacy-proof timelines have failed to improve.

Beeton and Case's review, identified in the supplied research as published on 23 July 2026, documents continuing needs for reproducible and standardized mucosal correlates, including for emerging respiratory viruses. It also describes unresolved, clear and reproducible correlates for live-attenuated influenza vaccines. This supplies contemporary evidence of specific scientific gaps without requiring the broader claim that existing correlates across all virology are predominantly virus-specific.

CIDRAP's 29 September 2026 universal-influenza-vaccine landscape update reports ongoing vaccine development, including two newly registered clinical trials. It does not directly assess whether the correlate problem has been solved. The supplied material covers the complete update page, rather than the complete underlying landscape, so continued development activity cannot by itself establish the absence of a successful correlate.

WHO's 7 April 2026 announcement describes R&D roadmaps for 10 viral families and a group of bacteria. This demonstrates a family-based approach to preparedness. The supplied announcement does not demonstrate a portable correlate, but the roadmap texts themselves were not supplied; their contents cannot be inferred from that omission.

Evidence boundary: the supplied review describes complete relevant CEPI materials and a complete Beeton–Case article obtained through alternative full-text XML, with no reported extraction truncation. Nevertheless, the Erbelding et al. 2018 strategic-plan text cited in the earlier research was absent, and the freshness search record was empty. These inputs substantiate dated achievements and specific remaining needs; they neither demonstrate completion of this innovation nor establish an exhaustive field-wide absence through 1 November 2026. Missing coverage is not evidence that an unexamined result is false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: for viruses from two viral families, freeze an immune measurement and prediction rule before clinical outcomes are unblinded, then show that they predict which vaccine regimens provide clinically meaningful human protection and which do not. Include at least one virus that had no accepted correlate when the measurement was proposed. Specify the endpoint, population, protection threshold, acceptable uncertainty and validation procedure in advance. The two-family threshold is a proposed milestone, not an established scientific or regulatory standard.
completion_criteria.label: Prospectively predict human vaccine protection across two viral families

completion_criteria.text: Proposed mechanistic requirement: accompany predictive success with evidence connecting the measured immune state causally to protection. The evidence should distinguish a protective process from a marker that merely accompanies it and explain the relationship to the chosen clinical endpoint. A post-hoc antibody titer associated with one successful trial would not meet the combined prospective and mechanistic requirement.
completion_criteria.label: Evidence connects the measured immune state causally to protection

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and boundary checks: independent teams should reproduce the assay and prospective predictions in additional cohorts or trials. Validation should report calibration, errors and uncertainty, including failures to transfer across populations, platforms, regimens or viruses. Success in two families would establish demonstrated breadth within those tests, not applicability to arbitrary viruses. Any claimed extension from severe-disease protection to infection or transmission prevention should receive its own validation.
completion_criteria.label: Independent teams reproduce assays and predictions with reported validation boundaries

completion_criteria.text: Proposed outbreak demonstration: use the measurement to support an epidemic deployment decision alongside adequate safety evidence and regulatory review, then confirm clinical protection through follow-up. Document whether the measurement supplied useful evidence in time to affect the decision and whether subsequent outcomes matched its predictions. This would test practical usefulness as well as predictive accuracy; it would not make safety assessment or clinical confirmation unnecessary.
completion_criteria.label: Inform epidemic deployment decisions with protection predictions confirmed through follow-up

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: VIR-04, protective immunity across a viral family, concerns the breadth of protection an intervention produces; VIR-09 concerns knowing whether protection will occur. A family-covering vaccine could provide a valuable test of a portable correlate, but efficacy breadth would not by itself prove predictive portability. VIR-05, durable respiratory-surface immunity that stops transmission, is especially relevant to selecting immune compartments and endpoints. A correlate of severe-disease protection would not establish completion of VIR-05.

Roster-based synthesis: VIR-01 predicts viral infectivity, transmission and escape from sequence, whereas VIR-09 predicts human vaccine protection from an immune measurement. Those predictions could inform each other, but their inputs and validation targets differ. VIR-08 seeks experimental understanding of viral genes without recognizable relatives; such discoveries could help explain protective mechanisms without themselves establishing a clinical correlate.

Roster-based synthesis: VIR-02 concerns empiric antiviral medicines; VIR-03 concerns elimination or permanent silencing of persistent viral genomes; and VIR-10 concerns sustained suppression by a conditionally replicating interfering particle. Their central outcomes are treatment, clearance, silencing or suppression. Immune measurements might help investigate some responses, but a vaccine-protection correlate would not establish those therapeutic outcomes. VIR-11 likewise requires evidence for an interruptible causal chain from persistent infection to chronic disease, beyond predicting vaccine protection.

Roster-based synthesis: VIR-06 seeks reliably prescribable bacteriophage therapy, and VIR-07 seeks viral delivery particles with chosen-cell targeting, repeat dosing and large genetic payloads. Both could benefit from better understanding of host immune responses, but their decisive challenges concern antibacterial treatment reliability and delivery performance, respectively. They remain distinct from a measurement that predicts human protection against a newly emerging virus.

unresolved_issues: The supplied freshness search record is empty, leaving exhaustive coverage through 1 November 2026 unverified.
The evidence does not identify a demonstrated measurement, prediction rule or causal mechanism meeting the full proposed capability; it also does not prove that none exists elsewhere.
The precise protective endpoint, target populations, assay, decision thresholds and acceptable uncertainty remain to be specified.
How much transfer across pathogens and vaccine platforms can be achieved without recalibration remains an open scientific question.
The full WHO roadmaps, complete underlying CIDRAP landscape and cited Erbelding et al. 2018 text were not supplied, limiting conclusions about their contents.
The two-family and outbreak-deployment demonstrations remain proposed milestones; their adequacy and regulatory usefulness have not been established by the supplied evidence.

brief.title: Early prediction of vaccine protection against new viruses
possible: During an outbreak, researchers could tell which vaccines are likely to protect people before enough illness outcomes are known. They would use an immune measurement and a prediction rule fixed in advance, backed by evidence explaining how the measured response helps protect people.

The approach would work across tested groups of related viruses, including a new virus without an accepted way to predict protection. Each prediction would specify what protection means, such as preventing infection or preventing severe illness.
why: Researchers could choose promising vaccine regimens earlier and stop pursuing ineffective ones. Public health officials could gain useful evidence about protection while an outbreak is still unfolding.
An approach that transfers across virus families could make outbreak preparation more reusable. Scientists would have less protection-prediction work to start from scratch when a new threat appears.

sources.showed: Their influenza vaccine update reports newly registered human trials and animal studies, including a vaccine that protected animals against several respiratory viruses.
sources.quote: vaccine delivered via nanoliposome carriers that elicited protective immunity against influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV infection in mouse, ferret, and cotton rat models, with antibody responses comparable to those induced by corresponding monovalent formulations.
sources.cited_for: The update documents continuing vaccine development and protection studies.
sources.not_established: Animal protection and new trials do not establish a measurement that predicts human protection across virus families.

sources.who: Komal Beeton and James Brett Case
sources.showed: Their review describes gaps in measuring protection at respiratory surfaces, such as the nose and airways. Reliable, standardized immune measurements remain unfinished work.
sources.quote: However, they often failed to consistently elicit robust immunity at mucosal sites.
sources.cited_for: Immune responses in blood may poorly represent protection at respiratory surfaces.
sources.not_established: The review does not establish a causal immune measurement that prospectively predicts human protection across virus families.

sources.who: Nicole Lurie and Kate Kelland at CEPI
sources.showed: They report that Serum Institute of India manufactured material for initial Bundibugyo vaccine trials in 14 days. Testing whether the vaccines protected people remained ahead.
sources.quote: The Serum Institute of India needed just 14 days to manufacture enough vaccine drug substance to begin the first trials of Oxford University’s ChAdOx Bundibugyo vaccine candidate.
sources.cited_for: Rapid vaccine production can coexist with unresolved questions about protection.
sources.not_established: Starting human trials does not establish clinical protection or an immune measurement that predicts it.

sources.showed: They developed research plans organized around virus families to coordinate pandemic preparedness.
sources.quote: WHO launched today, together with partners, research and development roadmaps for 10 viral families and a group of bacteria.
sources.cited_for: Preparedness research is being organized around families of related viruses.
sources.not_established: Organizing research by virus family does not demonstrate that a protection measurement transfers between families.

shown: Vaccine development can move quickly. CEPI reports that Bundibugyo vaccine trials began 80 days after the first reported case. Whether those vaccines protected people still required later testing.

Beeton and Case describe why predicting protection remains difficult for respiratory vaccines: immunity in blood can miss defenses in the airways. Reproducible measurements of protection at those surfaces remain an open research need.
missing: A fixed immune measurement and prediction rule that forecast human protection against a new virus before clinical outcomes are known.
Evidence that the measured immune response helps cause protection, rather than merely accompanying it.
Independent confirmation that the measurement and predictions work across tested virus families, populations and vaccine types.
An outbreak decision informed by an early prediction, with protection subsequently confirmed through follow-up.

milestones.label: Advance predictions succeed across two virus families
milestones.explanation: A measurement and rule fixed before outcomes are revealed would have to predict human protection across two virus families, including a virus without an accepted predictor. This would demonstrate useful prediction beyond a single family.

milestones.label: The measured immune response helps cause protection
milestones.explanation: Evidence would have to connect the measured immune response causally to the chosen form of protection. This would distinguish a protective process from a marker that merely accompanies it.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce results and establish their limits
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce the measurement and advance predictions in additional human studies, reporting errors, uncertainty and failures to transfer. This would establish where the approach can be trusted.

milestones.label: Outbreak decisions use predictions that follow-up confirms
milestones.explanation: A prediction would have to inform an outbreak vaccine deployment decision alongside safety evidence and regulatory review, with protection confirmed through follow-up. This would establish usefulness under outbreak conditions.

uncertain: How far can a protection measurement transfer between viruses and vaccine types without adjusting its prediction rule?
Which form of protection, populations and acceptable prediction errors should define success?
Would success across two virus families provide enough evidence for useful outbreak decisions?

page.title: Mechanistic correlates of protection across viral families
page.definition: An immune measurement and a fixed prediction rule predict human vaccine efficacy—the reduction in a specified clinical outcome caused by vaccination—for an emerging virus in a previously untested viral family. The measured immune function causally contributes to protection, and prediction precedes clinical outcome data from that virus.

goal.need: At the 100-day emergency mark, CEPI reported no approved Bundibugyo-specific vaccine in an account dated 25 August 2026 that was not peer reviewed. WHO's March 2026 Paramyxoviridae roadmap identifies undefined immune correlates and clinical endpoints as barriers to vaccine development and calls for validated measurements to support immunobridging, the inference of protection from immune responses.

statements.body: World Health Organization, Paramyxoviridae Research & Development Roadmap
statements.quote: Define quantitative and mechanistic correlates (including mucosal, humoral, and cellular immunity) supported by standardized assays to enable immunobridging and regulatory approval.
statements.context: A stated need for vaccine development within Paramyxoviridae.

statements.body: US National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases
statements.quote: characterize influenza immunity and correlates of immune protection
statements.context: A research objective in funding announcement PA-18-858 for universal influenza vaccine research.

statements.context: CEPI and PATH's programme to consolidate evidence on correlates for epidemic-prone viruses.

completion.title: A mechanistic correlate predicts human vaccine efficacy prospectively in a previously untested viral family.
completion.criterion: A peer-reviewed prospective human vaccine-efficacy study validates an immune measurement and an unchanged prediction rule transferred from another viral family, for an emerging virus without an accepted correlate when the rule was fixed. The rule predicts a prespecified clinical endpoint before its clinical outcomes are known, without calibration on that virus's efficacy data, and meets the protocol's prespecified predictive-validation criterion. Experimental evidence establishes the measured immune function as a cause of protection in the target setting.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; synthesis of published definitions, without an externally established combined completion test.
completion.basis: WHO publications, FDA surrogate-endpoint guidance, NIAID objectives and CEPI/Wellcome calls were searched for a test combining mechanism, prospective human prediction and transfer between viral families; none was found. This synthesis extends the published mechanistic-correlate and general-surrogate definitions to that transfer. These sources supply no universal numerical prediction-error cutoff; validation therefore requires a prespecified protocol criterion. Endpoint and platform dependence constrain transfer.

milestones.title: A measured immune function causally protects animals against a virus.
milestones.criterion: The measured immune function has a causal protective effect in the experimental system, meeting the mechanistic component of the mCoP definition. Human validity remains separate. McMahan et al., published on 4 December 2020, showed dose-dependent SARS-CoV-2 protection after transfer of purified convalescent IgG in 12 rhesus macaques, in four groups of three.
milestones.set_by: Plotkin and Gilbert's 2012 nomenclature and discussion of animal evidence; the laboratory component of their mechanistic correlate of protection definition.
milestones.threshold_quote: A CoP that is mechanistically and causally responsible for protection

milestones.title: An immune measurement predicts a virus-specific clinical endpoint in a defined human population.
milestones.criterion: An immune measurement varies among participants and is associated with a pathogen-specific clinical endpoint in a defined population. In the mRNA-1273 COVE analysis published on 23 November 2021, day 57 antibody markers were inversely associated with symptomatic COVID-19 risk; the vaccine-recipient analysis included 36 cases and 1,005 noncases.
milestones.set_by: Qin et al.'s 2007 three-tier framework, correlate-of-risk definition; retained in Plotkin and Gilbert's 2012 nomenclature.
milestones.threshold_quote: an association must be observed between these measurements and the pathogen-specific clinical end point.

milestones.title: An immune marker predicts vaccine efficacy within the original clinical setting.
milestones.criterion: A correlate of risk predicts vaccine efficacy in the original clinical setting. Under the statistical-surrogate criterion, conditioning on the marker removes the association between vaccination and the clinical endpoint. Qin et al.'s 2007 reanalysis of a 1943 influenza study, with 1,776 men and alternate allocation, supported Weiss strain A antibody titres: predicted efficacy against strain-specific influenza hospitalization was 82%, versus 73% observed (95% confidence interval 57–84%).
milestones.set_by: Gilbert, Qin and Self's 2008 framework, level 1 statistical surrogate of protection; no universal numerical accuracy cutoff.
milestones.threshold_quote: predicting vaccine efficacy for the same setting as the trial

milestones.title: An immune marker predicts vaccine efficacy across clinical settings.
milestones.criterion: A level 1 surrogate predicts vaccine efficacy in different settings, assessed using multiple efficacy trials or post-licensure studies and meta-analysis. Khoury et al., published on 17 May 2021, fitted normalized neutralization data from seven SARS-CoV-2 vaccines and one convalescent cohort and tested leave-one-out efficacy predictions. This supports bridging between vaccines against one virus; it does not establish transfer between viral families.
milestones.set_by: Gilbert, Qin and Self's 2008 framework, level 2 general surrogate of protection; different settings include populations and vaccine formulations, without requiring different viral families.
milestones.threshold_quote: predicting vaccine efficacy across different settings (building bridges)

not_found: No primary report was found demonstrating the combined prospective human, mechanistic and cross-family capability.
The full WHO/IVB/13.01 report could not be opened; its WHO publication page was accessible.
